GROUP:      flux-framework.org
KIND:       MiniCluster
VERSION:    v1alpha2

FIELD: spec <Object>


DESCRIPTION:
    MiniCluster is an HPC cluster in Kubernetes you can control
    Either to submit a single job (and go away) or for a persistent single- or
    multi- user cluster
    
FIELDS:
  archive	<Object>
    Archive to load or save

  backoffLimit	<integer>
    BackoffLimit is the number of retries for the job before failing

  cleanup	<boolean>
    Cleanup the pods and storage when the index broker pod is complete

  containers	<[]Object> -required-
    Containers is one or more containers to be created in a pod.
    There should only be one container to run flux with runFlux

  deadlineSeconds	<integer>
    Should the job be limited to a particular number of seconds?
    Approximately one year. This cannot be zero or job won't start

  flux	<Object>
    Flux options for the broker, shared across cluster

  interactive	<boolean>
    Run a single-user, interactive minicluster

  jobLabels	<map[string]string>
    Labels for the job

  logging	<Object>
    Logging modes determine the output you see in the job log

  maxSize	<integer>
    MaxSize (maximum number of pods to allow scaling to)

  minSize	<integer>
    MinSize (minimum number of pods that must be up for Flux)
    Note that this option does not edit the number of tasks,
    so a job could run with fewer (and then not start)

  network	<Object>
    A spec for exposing or defining the cluster headless service

  pod	<Object>
    Pod spec details

  services	<[]Object>
    Services are one or more service containers to bring up
    alongside the MiniCluster.

  shareProcessNamespace	<boolean>
    Share process namespace?

  size	<integer>
    Size (number of job pods to run, size of minicluster in pods)
    This is also the minimum number required to start Flux

  tasks	<integer>
    Total number of CPUs being run across entire cluster

outputs.summary: The scaling study of osu_allreduce from 1 to 5 nodes has been successfully completed. The latency of the MPI_Allreduce operation was measured for various message sizes at each scale. The results demonstrate a general trend of increasing latency with an increasing number of nodes, which is expected for collective communication operations. For smaller message sizes, the latency overhead is primarily due to synchronization costs, while for larger message sizes, it is dominated by data transfer time. The use of AWS EFA networking ensures low-latency and high-bandwidth, but the inherent complexity of the Allreduce algorithm, which requires all processes to participate, leads to increased communication time as more processes are added. The collected FOM matrices provide a clear view of this scaling behavior.

final_fom.reasons: The MPI Allreduce operation is a collective communication primitive that aggregates data from all processes and distributes the result back to all of them. Its performance is critical for many HPC applications. The observed increase in latency with more nodes is consistent with the logarithmic complexity of modern Allreduce algorithms (e.g., recursive doubling or ring-based approaches). As the number of nodes grows, the number of communication steps and the potential for network contention increase, leading to higher overall latency. The AWS EFA interconnect provides a low-latency, high-bandwidth fabric that mitigates these effects, but the fundamental scaling characteristics of the collective operation remain.
